picks.editorial_note: An AI model (Omnii) designed a bacteriophage used in the first-ever treatment of a patient with an antibiotic-resistant infection — a genuine first-in-human application of generative AI to therapeutic design, not just a lab demonstration.
picks.title: This time, the virus is on the patient’s side. AI helped design it

picks.editorial_note: CSIRO's AI-based imaging technique independently confirmed the iconic Event Horizon Telescope image of the M87 black hole in a Nature publication, giving major external validation to one of astrophysics' most famous results via machine learning.
picks.title: New CSIRO technique confirms iconic black hole image

picks.editorial_note: ARPA-H committed up to $53 million to an MIT-led team using generative AI to design next-generation herbicide alternatives — a large federal bet on AI-driven chemistry to solve a persistent agricultural and public-health problem.
picks.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop next-generation alternatives to modern weed killers

picks.editorial_note: A $19 million Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund grant will let Texas Tech build an AI-integrated computing cluster for chip simulation, reinforcing state-level investment in the AI-semiconductor pipeline.
picks.title: Texas Tech Receives $19 Million Grant to Further Semiconductor Innovation | Texas Tech Now

picks.editorial_note: Atos and Inria's strategic partnership to commercialize sovereign AI research (physical AI, agentic AI, robotics, cybersecurity) signals a notable industry-academia push toward European technological sovereignty.
picks.title: Atos and Inria enter into a strategic partnership to accelerate the transfer of research into sovereign industrial applications

picks.editorial_note: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit amid a national-security-linked scandal triggered a government investigation and industry uncertainty, with outsized implications for AI hardware supply and policy given Nvidia's central role in the field.
picks.title: Nvidia seeks successor after Jensen Huang's exit wobbles AI industry

picks.editorial_note: MIT CSAIL and CMU researchers' new 'Workspace Models' let robots retain and recall memory of past observations without costly retraining, a meaningful step toward more capable, general-purpose robotic learning.
picks.title: A new form of memory helps robots learn complex skills

picks.editorial_note: A new MIT quantization method targeting the KV cache bottleneck promises faster, more memory-efficient large language model inference — practical infrastructure work headed to NeurIPS that could cut real-world LLM serving costs.
picks.title: Faster data compression through quantization

picks.editorial_note: Science Tokyo's ZEBRA-Prop method lightens the computational cost of predicting material properties from language-model representations, an efficiency gain that could broaden AI's use in materials discovery.
picks.title: 言語モデルを用いた材料物性の予測を軽量化 | Science Tokyo - 東京科学大学

picks.editorial_note: UConn's symposium on a proposed $1 billion, 15-year AI investment in frontline social services surfaced serious policy concerns about how AI deployment could affect vulnerable communities, shaping the public debate on responsible AI rollout in social care.
picks.title: Experts Explore How AI Could Affect Vulnerable Communities, Social Service Providers - UConn Today
